Items.Authors: Christine Gregg, John C. Mather, Eliad Peretz, Othman Oudghiri-Idrissi, Omar M. Marey, Jamila Taaki, Stuart B. Shaklan, Ahmed Mohamed
Items.Title: Hybrid observatory for earthlike exoplanets: concepts for dynamically stable constructed starshades
Items.Abstract: The Hybrid Observatory for Earthlike Exoplanets (HOEE) is a mission concept that envisions imaging Earth-sized exoplanets around exoplanets using an earth-based telescope and orbiting starshade. To meet propulsion requirements, the starshade must meet stringent mass requirements while maintaining high levels of shape precision under station keeping loads during observation. In this paper, we describe robotic assembly concepts for a 100m starshade. We first characterize the anticipated dynamic structural requirements given anticipated station keeping loads required to keep the starshade aligned during an observation. We then analyze several structural designs suitable for robotic assem

Items.Authors: Jing Luo, Xu He, Shuyan Xu, Jihong Dong, Tianyi Zhang
Items.Title: Optical alignment and opto-mechanical integration of the China Space Station Telescope (CSST) optical telescope element
Items.Abstract: The Chinese Space Station Telescope (CSST) is a space-based observatory equipped with a 2-meter astronomical telescope. It is scheduled for launch in 2027. The Optical Telescope Element (OTE) of the CSST is a 2m off-axis three-mirror anastigmat optical system, whose field of view (FOV) is 1.1°×1°. The optical alignment poses a key difficulty for the OTE, due to the combination of non-parallel optical axes of all the three mirrors and the use of a freeform surface for the tertiary mirror. Whole-process deterministic optical alignment has been achieved successfully. The 2-meter-diameter primary mirror and the 4-meter main substrate were integrated with high precision, achieving an angular error of less than 10 arcseconds and a positional error under 0.05 mm. After integration and alignment, the OTE was tested in a vacuum chamber. The average RMS wavefront error over full FOVs was measured to be 0.074λ at 632.8 nm.

Items.Authors: Jean-François Sauvage, Pierre-Louis Mayeur, Cyril Petit, Nicolas Védrenne, Thierry Fusco
Items.Title: PROVIDENCE : a ground station for space observation
Items.Abstract: PROVIDENCE will be an ambitious optical research platform primarily dedicated to the observation of. It is a 2.5m adaptive telescope optimized for High Angular Resolution. Installed at the Observatoire de Haute Provence, the project targets dual applications, covering satellite and debris observation, astronomical observation, innovative instrumentation and cross-disciplinary issues around environmental and atmospheric characterization, laser focusing and optical telecoms (QKD and deep space communications). In this presentation, we give technical details on this station, flowing down from its science objectives to the technical specifications and functionalities. PROVIDENCE will embed high-level tracking capacities, will propose 2 Nasmyth and 4 Coudé foci allowing operational and research instrumentation. Currently at the study and prototyping stage, the station will be ready for the observation of the near-Earth asteroid APOPHIS in April 2029.

Items.Authors: Sam Ragland, Guido Brusa, Alessandro Cavallaro, Daniel Caywood, Laird Close, Juan Carlos Guerra, Michael Lefebvre, Douglas Miller, Mark Smithwright, Gregory Taylor, Christian Veillet, Xianyu Zhang, Roberto Biasi, Marlène de Sepibus, Daniele Gallieni, Jared Males, Elena Masciadri, Brandon Mechtley, Fernando Pedichini, Camilo Weinberger, Heejoo Choi, Guido Agapito, Matthieu Bec, Maria Bergomi, Al Conrad, Steve Ertel, Simone Esposito, Jamison Noenickx, David Munoz, Chang Jin Oh, Eliad Peretz, Enrico Pinna, Roberto Ragazzoni, Fabio Rossi, Joseph Shields
Items.Title: The path to agile extreme adaptive optics at the Large Binocular Telescope Observatory
Items.Abstract: We highlight recent exciting AO science and discuss ongoing efforts to elevate the AO systems to facility-class status, along with strategies to transform them into Agile Extreme Adaptive Optics (AgXAO) systems to operate effectively under harsh and variable seeing conditions.  We share lessons learned from recent service missions, including the critical effort to recover from water intrusion in one of the ASMs, where the magnet side of the thin shell was recoated. Additionally, we present the status of refurbishing the Magellan ASM to serve as a compatible spare for the LBT, including upgrades to the Magellan reference body, along with long-term mitigation plans to replace the entire ASM or its electronics with next-generation hardware. We present LBTO’s AO operations and technological advancements in the context of Extremely Large Telescopes, highlighting its role as a testbed for advanced wavefront control algorithms, astrophotonics experiments, and machine learning applications.

Items.Authors: Cyril Pannetier, Rafa Nadhil, Nazim Ali Bharmal, Alondra Solá, Kacem El Hadi, Myriam Rodrigues, Hermine Schnetler, Clarysse Picard
Items.Title: MOSAIC on ELT: current assessment of the project environmental footprint, from cradle to grave
Items.Abstract: MOSAIC, a multi-object spectrograph for the Extremely Large Telescope, is currently in its preliminary design phase (B2). In 2024, an initial carbon footprint estimate was conducted, offering rough CO₂eq emission figures but excluding key components like electronics, cryostats, and the AIT phase. In early 2026, a comprehensive life cycle analysis (LCA) was performed, aligning with ESA LCA Guidelines and covering all project phases—from early design to end-of-life. This updated study aims to provide the astrophysical community with robust environmental impact data, guide efforts to reduce the project’s ecological footprint, and establish a replicable methodology for future astronomical instruments. The analysis includes all recommended impact categories, ensuring a holistic assessment of MOSAIC’s environmental effects.

Items.Authors: Ryota Heibatake, Yoshiyuki Ando, Kaito Ozawa, Shutaro Ueda, Daisuke Yonetoku, Makoto Arimoto, Tatsuya Sawano, Kimiyoshi Ichikawa, Norio Tokuda, Yasuhiro Shoji, Shoya Matsuda, Satoshi Hatori, Kyo Kume, Shinko Sando, Satoshi Mizushima
Items.Title: Proton radiation damage experiments on diamond radiation detectors for a 3U-size CubeSat project
Items.Abstract: Charged particles (electrons, protons, and ions) in the Earth’s upper atmosphere can be accelerated along geomagnetic field lines and escape into space, yet their role in the Earth–space matter circulation remains unclear. Observational data E ~ 10 keV are limited, and polar energy flux contributes to non X-ray background for X-ray observations. We are developing a 3U CubeSat with diamond detectors developed by Kanazawa University. Au/Ti-electrode detectors developed by Kanazawa University and Element Six diamond were irradiated with 100 MeV protons (100-year equivalent) at the Wakasa Wan Energy Research Center, showing no degradation in linearity and energy resolution. We also assess thickness variants and modified structures (boron-doped surface, PIN: boron front/nitrogen back, and tantalum-doped) using radioisotope (e.g., 241Am) and β-ray (90Sr) measurements, comparing linearity and energy resolution before and after irradiation.

Items.Authors: Julien Lozi, Kyohoon Ahn, Vincent Deo, Olivier Guyon, Sandrine Juillard, Garima Singh, Sebastien Vievard
Items.Title: AO3k + SCExAO: on-sky wavefront quality and demonstration of novel WFS techniques with the double XAO system
Items.Abstract: SCExAO+AO3k serves both as a platform for high contrast imaging technology maturation and as a science instrument. They were recently upgraded to improve capabilities and support new developments. The system is evolving toward a tighter integration between multiple WFSs and AO stages of correction, with the first stage providing visible and NIR WFSing. It has been operational since October, demonstrating high stability on-sky in most seeing conditions. Having two XAO in series allows us to deploy advanced WFC techniques optimized for HCI (speckle nulling, EFC, LOWFS, F&F) on the second-stage XAO loop, as AO3k delivers high-contrast PSFs already. Areas of ongoing research include use of photonics for spectral interferometric sensing, PSF reconstruction from WFS telemetry, and non-linear sensors. We will present here on-sky HCI performance characterizations, and on-sky demonstrations of novel WFC techniques to improve the contrast behind the coronagraph.

Items.Authors: Ralf Jedamzik, Martin Kurz, Clemens Kunisch, Hauke Esemann, Claudia Stolz, Axel Ohlinger, Victor Alvan Amasifuen, Janina Krieg
Items.Title: Progress and upscaling of adhesive-free fused closed back ZERODUR® light weight structures
Items.Abstract: Lightweight mirror blanks for space applications must balance volume, weight, and stiffness to enable effective thermomechanical performance within rocket transport space restrictions. Closed back mirrors enable optimal performance at smaller overall Volume and reduced weight. Bonding the back with adhesives might affect the thermomechanical stability of the mirror.  SCHOTT has recently presented closed back ZERODUR® mirror blanks produced with adhesive-free fusing on 480 mm diameter scale. The quality of the fused interface enables a high degree of strength and almost monolithic quality in terms of stress birefringence and CTE homogeneity.   Meanwhile the technology moved forward on the path of maturing, being upscaled to almost meter sized structures and further characterization of properties.   This paper gives an update on the development of adhesive-free fusing of ZERODUR® structures with a focus on light weight closed back mirror blanks.

Items.Authors: Sungwook E. Hong, Jae-Woo Kim, Arman Shafieloo, Sang-Hyun Chun, Jeong-Yeol Han, Ho Seong Hwang, Yunjong Kim, Chung-Uk Lee, Changbom Park, David Parkinson, Jubee Sohn, Soung-Chul Yang
Items.Title: The Korea Large Spectroscopic Telescope (KLST) project for flux-limited spectroscopic survey in southern hemisphere
Items.Abstract: The Korea Large Spectroscopic Telescope (KLST) is planned as a next-generation facility utilizing twin 6.5m telescopes (effective 9.2m) located in Chile. KLST will conduct a flux-limited spectroscopic survey of the Southern sky, targeting all sources brighter than approximately r≈22 magnitude to secure an unprecedented galaxy sample up to z≈1.4. The primary science goals are precision cosmology (constraining dark energy and the origin of Inflation via primordial non-Gaussianity and clustering fossils) and deep Galactic Archaeology (EMP/CEMP stars, Magellanic Clouds AMR). The instrument features high-multiplex MOS (up to 13,000 fibers, R ≈6000/45,000) and a simultaneous IFS mode. Technical R&D focuses on a high-density Robotic Fiber Positioner System (RFPS) (requiring < 5μm precision) and segmented mirror technology development.

Items.Authors: Yang Huang, Chuanjie Zheng, Jifeng Liu
Items.Title: "Frog-eyes" in astronomy: monitoring binary radial velocity variations through a pair of narrow-band filters
Items.Abstract: We propose the "Frog-eyes" system, which employs a pair of narrow-band filters: one positioned near a strong absorption line to capture signals from Doppler shifts, and the other placed on the adjacent continuum to monitor intrinsic variations. The combination of observations from the two filters enables the extraction of radial velocity (RV) curves from a large sample of binary stars, and is particularly efficient for single-lined binaries (SB1), using photometric techniques. With a typical ground-based photometric precision of approximately 0.3%, the uncertainties in the derived semi-amplitude K and eccentricity e are less than 10% and 0.1, respectively, for binary systems with K > 30 km/s. Once this system is properly installed on large-field-of-view survey telescopes, the rate of acquiring RV curves for binaries will approach their detection rate in leading time-domain photometric surveys.

Items.Authors: Matheus J. Castro, Julian Stürmer, Stanimir Letchev, Jacob Pember, Andreas Seifahrt, Lars A. Buchhave
Items.Title: 2ES: the development of a solar telescope
Items.Abstract: For the past decade, many solar telescopes (ST) feeds have been implemented for Extreme Precision Radial Velocity (EPRV) spectrographs. These telescopes observe the Sun on a daily basis in order to monitor instrument stability, performance and radial velocity (RV) precision. The ongoing development of the Second Earth Spectrograph (2ES) aims to measure the stellar RV signals on the order of ~10 cm/s; thus continuous solar observations become essential to ensure that the spectrograph achieves its designed precision. A dedicated ST is therefore a critical component of the overall 2ES program.  The 2ES-ST is designed for fully autonomous operation under -harsh- environmental conditions throughout the five-year 2ES operation plan. This paper presents the current status of the telescope’s development, describing the optical, optomechanical and electronic subsystems, as well the software framework implemented for automated observations and communication with the main 2ES server.

Items.Authors: Carlos Enrique Rodriguez Alvarez, Andreas Kelz, Daniel Sablowski, Isabelle Guinouard, Cyril Pannetier, Audrey A. Lanotte
Items.Title: 3D-printed vs lithographic microlens arrays: a scientific evaluation for MOSAIC and astronomical applications
Items.Abstract: The focus of this work is the analysis and evaluation of the suitability of 3D-printed microlens arrays (MLAs) for use in astronomical instrumentation, in particular for the MOSAIC Multi-Object Spectrograph. This study is based on a theoretical comparison between conventionally manufactured microlenses and 3D-printed microlenses, complemented by a laboratory characterization and performance comparison between two similar 19-microlens arrays.

Items.Authors: Genoveva Micheva, Roelof S. de Jong, Joar G. Brynnel, Roland Winkler, Olga Bellido-Tirado, Steffen Frey, Andreas Kelz, Jonathan Irwin, Walter Seifert, Ingo Stilz, Alexander Pramskiy, Florence Laurent, Michael Lehmitz, Mark Cunningham, Wolfgang Gaessler, Jens-Kristian Krogager, Gérard Zins, Thomas Szeifert, Ioannis Politopoulos, Ramon Navarro, Sabine Bellstedt, Peter M. Weilbacher, Michael J. Irwin, Weijia Sun, Marica Valentini
Items.Title: 4MOST commissioning results
Items.Abstract: 4MOST completed a continuous 60-day commissioning campaign, bringing the facility to scientific readiness. We verified all top-level requirements under real operating conditions via intensive night tests and daily calibration analysis. Instrumental stability, throughput, and data quality were characterised using radial-velocity and spectrophotometric standards, white dwarfs, benchmark stars, clusters, and galaxies. A validated twilight strategy enabled observations of very bright stars (G<7m). Throughput was mapped vs. fiber tilt, altitude, rotator angle, seeing, and airmass. Faint-end performance was probed by stacking 20min exposures to emulate deep integrations. Attached nighttime calibrations were contaminated by sky targets, so we redesigned the wavelength-calibration strategy and updated the pipeline. All templates and ETC predictions were validated. We also present the commissioning data flow, challenges encountered, and lessons learned for survey operations.

Items.Authors: Andreas Kelz, Allar Saviauk, Thomas Jahn, Dennis Plüschke, Walter Seifert, Florence Laurent, Jean-Emmanuel Migniau, Scott Smedley, Jonathan Irwin
Items.Title: 4MOST fiber system: integration, verification, and commissioning
Items.Abstract: 4MOST is a multi-object spectroscopic survey facility for the VISTA telescope with a large multiplex achieved by over 2400 optical fibers. The entire instrument has been installed and commissioned at ESO’s Paranal observatory in 2025.   This paper presents the complex installation of the 27m long science fibers from the positioner at the focal plane, through the Cassegrain Cable Wrap, to the high and the two low-resolution spectrographs below the Azimuth floor. In addition, various auxiliary fiber systems were installed and verified, which include simultaneous calibration fibres, mini-fiber-bundles for acquisition and guiding, fiducial fibers for reference, and a back-illumination of all fibers for metrology purpose. The paper presents the on-sky performance of the fiber system based on the commissioning results, which feature 812 spectra for each spectrograph.

Items.Authors: Steffen Frey, Thomas Liebner, Roland Winkler, Daniel Sablowski, Roelof de Jong, Jérôme Amiaux, Diogo Rio Fernandes, Laura Cediel Ramos, Carlos Rodriguez, Paško Roje, Allar Saviauk, Florence Laurent
Items.Title: 4MOST focal surface alignment
Items.Abstract: The 4MOST instrument achieved first light on VISTA at Paranal in October 2025. Challenges during MAIT/AIT included precise alignment and verification of focal surface components prior to delivery to Chile, requiring a complex workflow, test stands, metrology tools like laser tracker, confocal sensors, large linear stages and star projection. Lessons learned offer guidance for future large multi object spectroscopic instruments.

Items.Authors: Florence Laurent, Didier Boudon, Eric Daguisé, Rémi Giroud, Aurélien Jarno, Alexandre Jeanneau, Andreas Kelz, Jens-Kristian Krogager, Victor Mauger-Vauglin, Jean-Emmanuel Migniau, Matthew Lehnert, Arlette Pécontal, Emmanuel Pécontal, Alban Remillieux, Johan Richard, Allar Saviauk
Items.Title: 4MOST low resolution spectrographs characterization in Chile
Items.Abstract: 4MOST is a fibre-fed spectroscopic facility on ESO’s VISTA telescope at Paranal, designed for large-scale surveys in galactic archaeology, high-energy astrophysics, galaxy evolution, and cosmology. Operated by a European–Australian consortium led by AIP, it achieved first light on 18 October 2025. The system deploys 2436 fibres across a 4.1 deg² field to feed two low-resolution spectrographs (1624 fibres, 370–950 nm, R > 4000) and one high-resolution spectrograph (812 fibres, ~44–69 nm per arm, R > 18000). The low-resolution spectrographs, built by CRAL, use an off-axis Schmidt collimator, three-arm dichroic splitting, and fast F/1.73 cameras with 6k × 6k CCD detectors. Following ESO’s provisional acceptance in May 2025, the low-resolution spectrographs were shipped to Chile, reassembled, realigned, and installed on VISTA. The referenced paper details their assembly, integration, performance validation, and the optimized procedures developed to meet top-level requirements in Chile.

Items.Authors: Walter Seifert, Wenli Xu, Carmen Feiz, Andreas Quirrenbach, Florian Rothmaier, Allar Saviauk, Andreas Kelz, Joar Brynnel, Jonathan Irwin, Mike Irwin
Items.Title: 4MOST: AITV of the high-resolution-spectrograph at ESO Paranal Observatory
Items.Abstract: 4MOST (4-meter Multi-Object Spectroscopic Telescope) is a wide-field, fiber-fed, high-multiplex spectroscopic survey facility and was installed in 2025 on the 4-meter ESO telescope VISTA in Chile. The 4MOST facility including is presently in commissioning phase. 4MOST will start regular science observation early 2026.  The back-end consists of one high-resolution spectrograph (HRS) and two identical low-resolution spectrographs.     The 4MOST HRS allows for simultaneous observations of up to 812 targets on a hexagonal 4.4 square degrees field of view at a spectral resolution R>18,000 covering 393 to 679nm in three channels.     In this paper, we present in detail the re-integration, alignment and tests of the HRS at the ESO integration facility. The results of the tests, the installation at the VISTA telescope and the final performance data of the fully integrated system are discussed.

Items.Authors: Jens-Kristian Krogager, Johan Richard, Florence Laurent, Mark Cunningham, Jonathan Irwin
Items.Title: 4MOST: on-sky performance of the Low Resolution Spectrographs (LRS)
Items.Abstract: 4MOST, the 4m Multi Object Spectroscopic Telescope, is an optical, fibre-fed, MOS facility for the VISTA telescope at ESO's Paranal Observatory in Chile. Its main science drivers are in the fields of galactic archeology, high-energy physics, galaxy evolution and cosmology. 4MOST recently received its first light in October 2025 and is starting operations in 2026. Here we present the results of on-sky tests obtained on the two low-resolution spectrographs (1624 fibres, three arms, 370-950 nm, R > 4000) which were constructed under the responsibility of CRAL. A special emphasis is put on the on-sky performance in terms of spectral resolution, cross-talk, sensitivity, and our efforts to characterize the instrument focus after installation on the telescope.

Items.Authors: Nyasha J. Suliali, James M. Ivory, Jon Mason, Manish R. Patel
Items.Title: A 50° full field of view imaging lens design for in-orbit UV wavelength sensing by a scientific CMOS sensor
Items.Abstract: The study of planetary atmospheres through optical imaging is a growing field in space science as humanity seeks to understand life on planets of our solar system. While reflective and catadioptric telescopes have largely dominated space-based imaging instruments, refractive telescopes still provide optical systems with f-numbers suitable to perform UV-based sensing such as investigating atmospheric composition and habitability. An all-spherical lens design suitable for in-orbit imaging of low-albedo planets such as Mars is presented in this work. The lens images a 50° full field of view at f/4.9, with a < 3.5 µm spot size suitable for a 10 µm pixel pitch CMOS sensor for scientific imaging in the UV-A, B and C wavelength range. An analysis of its aberrations and optical performance is presented with reference to requirements for imaging low-albedo planets such as Mars.

Items.Authors: Xiaoming Zhu
Items.Title: A compact, ultra-high resolution VIPA spectrograph for solar observations: astrocomb characterization and first light
Items.Abstract: This study presents a compact, fiber-fed spectrograph using a Virtually Imaged Phased Array (VIPA). Calibrated by a 25 GHz astrocomb, it operates from 592.76 to 657.07 nm with a spectral resolution of 290,000–340,000 and an asymmetric instrumental profile best fit by a Fano-Lorentz function. On-sky tests at the New Vacuum Solar Telescope successfully detected solar five-minute oscillations, resolved magnetic broadening in sunspots, and provided the first ground-based identification of the faint Si I line within Hα. These results validate the VIPA as a promising, compact platform for high-resolution solar spectroscopy.

Items.Authors: Shidong Shen, Hua Bai
Items.Title: A conceptual design for the alignment system of JUST
Items.Abstract: Jiao Tong University Spectroscopic Telescope(JUST) is of great significance to Chinese astronomy. The 4.4-meter primary mirror of JUST will adopt segmented mirror active optics to realize co-focus in optica and near-infrared bands. The alignment system will use several Shack-Hartmann based measurement techniques to position piston, tip-tilt of the segments, secondary mirror rigid body motion to correctly align the JUST. We present a conceptual design of the alignment system including the requirements, alignment modes, predicted performance, and an optical design.

Items.Authors: Ruben J. Diaz
Items.Title: A decade of instrument and observing mode usage at the Gemini Observatory
Items.Abstract: Gemini operates a suite of facility and visiting instruments that support a wide range of observing modes, from seeing-limited and speckle imaging to AO imaging, AO coronography, and spectroscopic techniques including longslit, multi-object and integral-field spectroscopy. Over the past decade, this suite—complemented by a world-class target-of-opportunity system—has enabled broad scientific productivity across both Gemini telescopes. This comprehensive analysis of instrument and observing-mode usage is based on photon-collecting time from the last ten years, examines how the astronomical community has used the available capabilities, and compares usage patterns with historical demand projections. These trends are compared to scientific publication metrics as indicators of productivity. Our goal is to provide an empirical reference for future instrumentation strategy at the Observatory and in particular to teams developing new instruments.

Items.Authors: Qiqige Xin, Jean-Louis Lizon, Bin Yu, Dinghao Feng, Mingda Jiang
Items.Title: A different opto-mechanical approach for CHORUS high resolution spectrograph
Items.Abstract: The Canary High Optical Resolution Ultra-stable Spectrograph (CHORUS) is a high resolution spectrographic facility for the GTC in La Palma. The facility includes an ultra stable spectrograph for radial velocity measurements: CHORUS VIS for Visible Band Spectrograph. If some important sub-systems like the detector cryostats and the echelle mosaic are direct heritage from ESPRESSO, the mechanical design departs from the one of the ESO VLT instrument. The paper documents how this design shall for example offer a longer vacuum autonomy without active pumping. The design of the optical bench as well as the implantation of the various optical components should also guaranty an easy and straight forward alignment.

Items.Authors: Auxiliadora Padrón-Brito, Natalia Arteaga-Marrero, Adrián Sánchez-Chaves, Diego Tamayo-Guzmán, Max Johann Dobat, Nicolas Lodieu, Jeff Kuhn
Items.Title: A focal-plane wavefront sensor based on a short multimode fiber and machine learning
Items.Abstract: The Small ELF (SELF) prototype for the Exo-Life Finder requires precise co-phasing and real-time correction of atmospheric wavefront errors. Conventional pupil-plane sensors suffer from non-common-path aberrations, motivating focal-plane wavefront sensing (FPWFS). We investigate a compact FPWFS concept based on a short multimode fiber (MMF). The modal interference within a centimeter-scale MMF produces an output intensity pattern able to distinguish the sign of even phase distributions that are degenerate in conventional imaging at the focal plane. A lightweight CNN retrieves low-order aberrations with millisecond-level inference, as confirmed by simulations. The approach is passive, low-cost, mechanically stable, and easy to integrate, offering a promising solution for narrow-field astronomical applications such as SELF/ELF, as well as for free-space optical communication systems employing narrowband beacons.

Items.Authors: Jean-Louis Lizon, Qiqige Xin
Items.Title: A full A-thermalization for the CHORUS UV spectrograp
Items.Abstract: The Canary High Optical Resolution Ultra-stable Spectrograph (CHORUS) includes a medium resolution spectrograph operating in the UV band. For obvious reasons this part of the facility is installed directly under the Nasmyth platform and therefore exposed to the strong temperature variations of the telescope dome. The paper describes how the design has been implemented to reduce as much as possible the thermal effect. In addition to an efficient thermal insulation the instrument is fully a-thermalized from its entrance slit up to the detectors. Beside the a-thermalization of the main optic train the paper details the opto-mechanical design of the two cameras. The lens are there mounted with a full radial and axial A-thermalization.

Items.Authors: Han Gao, Chunyan Wang, Hao Yang, Zhixu Wu, Zhengyang Li
Items.Title: A high-precision alignment method for astronomical optical telescopes using structured lasers
Items.Abstract: To address image degradation in optical telescopes with fast focal ratios—a problem caused by the misalignment of optical elements during assembly and observation—this study proposes a high-precision calibration method for image quality detection and correction. The method substitutes parallel laser beams for starlight to generate the incident wavefront required for calibration. Low-order aberrations resulting from system misalignment are calculated from the centroid coordinate offsets of laser spots on defocused planes, thereby enabling feedback-controlled alignment adjustments. Simulations and experiments were conducted on a single parabolic mirror system with a diameter (D) of 500 mm and a focal ratio of F/3. The results indicate that for mirror tilt misalignments ranging from −2◦ to +2◦, the estimated error for the Zernike coefficients Z4–Z6 is below 0.1λ (λ = 650 nm).

Items.Authors: Flavio C. Cruz, Marlon M. Correia, Tomas P. V. Andrade, Henrique Lupinari, Colby Jurgenson, Andrew Szentgyorgyi
Items.Title: A laser frequency comb for calibration of G-CLEF: preliminary results
Items.Abstract: The GMT-Consortium Large Earth Finder (G-CLEF) is a fiber-fed, optical echelle spectrograph that will be a first light instrument for the Giant Magellan Telescope (GMT). G-CLEF will have a precision radial velocity (PRV) goal of 10 cm/sec in the highest resolution mode (R = 110 k). It will operate in a blue (350 to 540 nm) and a red (540 to 950 nm) channel, each with its own camera optics and detector. This paper will provide an overview of the laser frequency comb, under development, that is one of the components of G-CLEF’s Advanced Wavelength Calibration System (AWCS). Its purpose it to provide a stable wavelength reference for characterizing and mitigating broadband chromatic drifts known to occur in Fabry-Perot cavities.

Items.Authors: Skyler Palatnick, Ryan Hersey, Maxwell Millar-Blanchaer, J. Kent Wallace, Tobias Wenger
Items.Title: A metasurface scalar vortex for the SCALES instrument
Items.Abstract: As scalar vortex coronagraphic mask development progresses with the long term goal of use in the Habitable Worlds Observatory, new opportunities for on-sky installation have emerged. With a metasurface platform, scalar vortices can overcome limitations of commonly used vector vortices. We describe development of a K-band metasurface scalar vortex for the SCALES instrument to be commissioned on Keck Observatory later this year. We report on device design, fabrication, and characterization, a vortex composed of silicon nanoposts on silica substrate. The device demonstrates high transmission and achromatic phase across the K band. We discuss simulated coronagraphic performance and plans for installation, future lab-characterization, and on-sky characterization. Upon installation, this optic will be the first scalar vortex, first charge-4 vortex, and first metasurface coronagraphic mask on-sky. Such a milestone will help pave the way for future metasurface coronagraphic instruments.

Items.Authors: Jake Zimmer
Items.Title: A novel high channel count thermal control system for precision astronomy
Items.Abstract: We present a compact, high-precision thermal control system that achieves an unusually high channel count in a modular, reconfigurable architecture. The HISPEC implementation provides 40 heater outputs and 80 temperature-sensor inputs in a low-profile rack-mount enclosure, addressing thermal-control demands that exceed the capabilities of traditional Lakeshore controllers or detector-controller–based solutions. The system architecture utilizes a backplane into which dedicated heater or sensor cards are inserted to tailor functionality while minimizing new hardware development. Heater cards support both low-power linear outputs for fine temperature trimming and high-power switching outputs for rapid warm-up. Sensor cards accommodate RTD and diode with programmable current sources and true 24-bit ADCs. Control and telemetry are provided over TCP/IP with integrated fault-handling. Although developed for HISPEC, this architecture is applicable to many thermally controlled instruments.

Items.Authors: Sara M. Simon
Items.Title: A novel scan strategy for large aperture telescope observations
Items.Abstract: The Simons Observatory (SO) Large Aperture Telescope (LAT) is a ~6 m crossed-Dragone telescope located at an elevation of 5200 m in the Atacama Desert in Chile. The LAT observes the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) with over 60,000 detectors and frequency coverage in six bands ranging from 24-315 GHz. Typically scan strategies for LATs in Chile have targeted patches on the sky that cover a fraction of the observable sky, but additional science cases have motivated new, wide observation strategies with ~daily cadences. We will describe the on-sky testing of these novel strategies.

Items.Authors: Ciro Del Vecchio, Vincenzo Greco, Alejandro Fernández Soler
Items.Title: A novel STOP Analysis computation: the Ariel case
Items.Abstract: The finite element model (FEM) for optically processing the  deformation field of a telescope structure allows for the calculation  of all optically relevant data within a single simulation run. This  paper focuses on a method for computing the impact of structural  deformations on ray tracing for the Ariel Space Telescope. These  deformations arise from external factors such as the gravity field  during ground tests and thermal distortions during operational  observations.    Once the ray tracing calculations are completed, the resulting  data is processed to estimate key optical performance metrics,  including the collimated beam, aberrations, spot diagram,  and point spread function. The method presented in this paper,  which is based on a multi-physics approach, effectively addresses  classical geometrical optics challenges once the structural mechanics  solution is obtained. This makes it an ideal tool for a comprehensive  Structural-Thermal-Optical Performance (STOP) analysis.

Items.Authors: Francisco Garzón, Roberto López, Enrique Joven, José Luis Rasilla, Fabio Tenegi
Items.Title: A proposal of a new multi-band imager and spectrograph for the GTC
Items.Abstract: Following GRANTECAN’s request for the procurement of a new instrument, the IAC is leading a consortium of institutions that will first develop the instrument concept and subsequently carry out its design, construction, and testing.    The concept presented in this contribution follows GRANTECAN’s specifications closely: a large imager and spectrograph capable of simultaneously covering, in either mode, the full spectral range from the ultraviolet to the K band, i.e. from 350 to 2500 nm. This will be achieved by splitting the incoming light with a set of dichroic mirrors into eight separate arms: four for the near‑infrared part of the spectrum (zY, J, H, K) and four for the visible range (U, B, V, RI). The imaging field of view will be 3 × 3 arcmin. The spectrograph section will consist of a large IFU with 18 slices, covering a common area of 10 × 9 arcsec for all eight arms, and a dispersive grating at the entrance of each arm.

Items.Authors: Olivier Daigle, Émile Beaulieu, Deren Mehmet, Hank Hu
Items.Title: A space qualified digital imaging platform: design, TVAC characterization, and radiation performance with the HWK4123 sCMOS sensor
Items.Abstract: We present the characterization results of Nüvü Camēras’ space qualified digital imaging platform, integrated with the Fairchild Imaging’s low noise (<0.25e RMS) HWK4123 9.4-megapixel sCMOS sensor. The imaging system has been designed for challenging missions requiring low read noise and/or high dynamic range, such as SSA, transient imaging or applications requiring daytime and nighttime imaging capability. Environmental testing was performed in TVAC to evaluate performance stability over the imaging system’s full temperature range. In addition, we present radiation response data obtained during a proton irradiation campaign conducted at TRIUMF (British Columbia, Canada), focusing on TID, and single-event phenomena observed in the HWK4123 sensor. These results demonstrate the suitability of the Nüvü Camēras-Fairchild Imaging innovative devices for space missions requiring high-performance wide-field sensing.

Items.Authors: Zhiyi Wang, Junlin Ma, Zhengqi Sun, Yunzhu Yang, Xiaopeng Feng, Jianli Wang
Items.Title: A unified metrology-to-adjustment framework for flatness optimization in large mosaic focal plane assemblies
Items.Abstract: This project develops a 2.5-meter wide-field astronomical telescope for near-Earth asteroid detection, space-debris surveillance, and high-cadence time-domain sky surveys. The system reaches 21-mag sensitivity with a field of view over 3 degrees in the 0.42–0.8 μm band, enabling rapid wide-area monitoring. It supports high-speed tracking with azimuth and elevation velocities of 15°/s and 6°/s while maintaining fine tracking precision at the 10⁻⁴–10⁻² °/s level. Its rapid angular-acceleration capability ensures accurate tracking of fast-moving targets.  The telescope integrates advanced optical design, precision opto-mechanics, a lightweight rigid structure, and a robust servo-control platform to ensure stable imaging and long-term reliability. It serves planetary-defense warning, space-situational awareness, transient detection, and time-domain astrophysics, demonstrating strong scientific, engineering, and strategic value.

Items.Authors: Massinissa Hadjara, Marcos Diaz, Hangxin Ji, Qinyang Dong, Mustapha Meftah, Florentin Millour, Bernard Foing
Items.Title: A.S.T.R.O.N.A.U.T: Astronomical Satellite for Tracking, Research, Observation, Nano-spacecraft, and Ultra-precision Astronomy Technology
Items.Abstract: The A.S.T.R.O.N.A.U.T project is an international initiative led by the Space and Planetary Exploration Laboratory (SPEL, University of Chile) in collaboration with partners from China and France. Its goal is to develop miniaturized satellites equipped with advanced instrumentation for high-precision space observations and long-term planetary exploration. A key component of the project investigates biological processes for future sustainable life-support systems on the Moon and Mars. In March 2026, SPEL will deploy CubeSats to study seed germination and extremophilic microorganisms aboard the International Space Station. Parallel experiments at the Chinese Space Station is highly suitable. In parallel, the project develops nanosatellites optimized for astronomy, targeting transients, exoplanets, and variable stars. A.S.T.R.O.N.A.U.T strengthens China–Chile cooperation while advancing both space biology and ultra-precision space-based astronomy.

Items.Authors: Justin R. Fletcher
Items.Title: Active optomechanical control for interferometric wavefront shaping in hybrid optical telescopes
Items.Abstract: Direct imaging of Earth-like exoplanets would enable unambiguous detection of the chemical signatures of exoplanetary  life. To form such an image, even for nearby planetary systems, an astronomical instrument must be sensitive to  1e−9 contrast while achieving an angular resolution on the order of 10 milliarcseconds. Fizeau optical interferometric telescopes that employ lightweight primary optical support structures may satisfy these challenging requirements at a feasible cost, but only if they are able to sustain differential motion of ~1 wave of error between the primaries. To address this optomechanical control task, we introduce and evaluate several visuomotor control approaches that enable both closed-loop correction of differential motion and controlled interferometric nulling to improve contrast.

Items.Authors: Jake Zimmer
Items.Title: Adapting PMSMs for precision cryogenic mechanisms
Items.Abstract: We present a general technique for adapting commercial off-the-shelf permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) for high-precision cryogenic actuation. Compared to stepper and piezoelectric solutions which face trade-offs between force, precision, travel, and power dissipation, modified PMSMs offer high torque and long-range articulation with reduced risk of resonance. Using modern high-resolution magnetic encoders, we achieve precise direct-drive positioning while avoiding encoder-related light leaks. Closed-loop operation with balanced loads enables exceptionally low holding currents due to the reduced cogging typical of PMSMs, lowering thermal loads within the cryogenic vacuum environment. This approach is being implemented in Caltech's detector characterization facility for NASA's UVEX mission, supporting mechanisms such as filter wheels, apertures, and deployable cryogenic masks that require a combination of high force, low power, and precise positioning.

Items.Authors: Changhui Rao, Lingxiao Li, Youming Guo, Zibo Ke
Items.Title: Adaptive optics design for China’s 14.5-m optical–infrared telescope system
Items.Abstract: The 14.5-m telescope ranks among the world’s largest, but its imaging is strongly limited by atmospheric turbulence. Achieving near-diffraction-limited resolution therefore requires adaptive optics (AO), which senses and corrects wavefront distortions in real time. To ensure sufficient sky coverage for AO, artificial laser guide stars—especially sodium guide stars—provide stable wavefront references when natural stars are sparse. The AO system comprises four subsystems: a laser guide star module, a wavefront sensing module, a wavefront correction module, and a wavefront control module. Aberrations measured from a natural or laser guide star are sent to the control module, which commands a tip–tilt mirror and deformable mirror to close the loop at high speed. This integrated approach mitigates turbulence, restores image sharpness toward the diffraction limit, and substantially improves the scientific productivity of the large telescope.

Items.Authors: Vincenzo Cianniello, Vincenzo De Caprio, Christian Eredia, Enrico Cascone
Items.Title: Additive Manufacturing to support mechanical design & advanced prototyping in the INAF 3DL@b
Items.Abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) is increasingly playing a strategic role in the design and production of mechanical structures for astronomical applications, due to its ability to produce components rapidly, with topologically optimized geometries and a high degree of functional integration. Modern astronomical infrastructures, require mechanical systems characterized by high ratio of optimization in terms of geometry, accuracy and thermo-mechanical stability. A particularly significant advantage is the ability to accelerate the prototyping process, allowing rapid validation of different structural layouts. In the Astronomical Observatory of Naples, the 3DL@b has been created, in the framework of the National Recovery and Resilience Plan project "STILES - Strengthening the Italian leadership in ELT and SKA". In this article is reported the cases study of MUAM (Moon UV Albedo Measurement) and the prototyping activities on MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations).

Items.Authors: Marta Maria Civitani, Gabriele Vecchi, Carolyn Atkins, Marcell Westsik
Items.Title: Additively manufactured fused-silica lightweight mirrors for high-resolution astronomical optics
Items.Abstract: The challenge of manufacturing astronomical optics is to provide both high spatial resolution imaging and large collecting area by means of low-mass mirrors. Recent advancements in Additive Manufacturing (AM), or 3D printing, of fused silica offer the potential to meet this challenge. AM allows for the incorporation of advanced lightweighting features which help preserve mirror shape accuracy and reduce the overall mass compared to traditional methods that require extensive material removal. Previous research confirmed that AM fused silica can be polished to the necessary sub-nanometer roughness for astronomical use. This work aims to extend those findings to high-energy astronomy applications. A simplified cylindrical mirror segment was 3D printed in three design variants: solid, TPMS-latticed, and Voronoi-latticed. This paper focuses on the metrological and manufacturing results, demonstrating that 3D printed fused silica is a promising substrate for future telescope mirrors.

Items.Authors: Carolin Rothhardt, Sylvio Klose, Pascal Birckigt, Stefan Schwinde, Ralph Schlegel, Stefan Risse
Items.Title: Advanced joining technologies for space for the fabrication of a 4-channel glass beamsplitter
Items.Abstract: Spaceborne optical instruments demand joining technologies to withstand vacuum, cryogenic temperatures, thermal gradients, and launch loads. We report the development of a Kösters prism beam splitter that separates a telescope beam into four infrared channels (800–1700 nm) on a single detector for a small satellite transient astronomy mission. The system comprises six aligned fused silica prisms, joined in three pairs. Prior to bonding, 3 µm dichroic beam splitter coatings are sputtered onto one prism in each pair. To achieve high mechanical stability down to 140 K and prevent interfacial absorption, the prisms are joined by plasma activated bonding. The three prism pairs are separated by vacuum gaps that implement total internal reflection, forming the four channels on different detector areas. These gaps are defined by silicate bonding of the prism pairs to a glass base plate. Coordinate metrology confirms high precision alignment throughout the assembly.

Items.Authors: Alejandro Garcia Cañas, Paloma Lopez Reyes, Nuria Gutierrez Luna, Francesc Valls-Vicent, Ana Iglesias Moreno, Carlos Honrado-Benítez, Emily Witt, Brian Fleming, Nicholas Kruczek, Emily Farr, Luis Rodriguez de Marcos, Kevin France, Juan Ignacio Larruquert
Items.Title: Advanced LUV/FUV multilayer coating for next-generation space observatories
Items.Abstract: The Lyman- and far ultraviolet (LUV, FUV: 90–200 nm) contains critical atomic and molecular diagnostics for planetary atmospheres and the circumgalactic medium. Future observatories such as NASA’s HWO depend on coatings optimized in this range. However, key spectral lines (e.g., O VI, N V, Si III, O I) are often obscured by the bright of Lyman-α line at 121.6 nm. The Juniper CubeSat mission concept (John Hopkins University and the University of Colorado) seeks to minimize Ly-α scatter for this reason. Motivated by this we present an innovative reflective notch-filter coating.  We also report recent developments in LUV/FUV coatings, including FUV band-pass mirrors with 4–40 nm bandwidths based on periodic and aperiodic fluoride multilayers. These technologies will be flight-tested on the FLUID sounding rocket as a pathfinder for HWO.

Items.Authors: Xianyu Zhang, Guido Brusa, Alessandro Cavallaro, Juan Carlos Guerra, Michael Lefebvre, Douglas Miller, John Prothro, Sam Ragland, Dan Rapoza, Manu Singh, Gregory Taylor, Michael Wagner
Items.Title: Advancements in monitoring and control of the adaptive secondary mirrors at the Large Binocular Telescope
Items.Abstract: This paper presents several key upgrades to the Adaptive Secondary Mirrors (ASMs) at the Large Binocular Telescope aimed at improving system reliability, safety, and adaptive optics (AO) performance. In the context of ASM performance, we developed an enhanced actuator monitoring system that provides more detailed and timely diagnostics, and a new tool for assessing mirror flat quality allowing earlier detection of surface issues. To improve the ASMs integration with the telescope, we introduced a PLC system for the ASMs, currently used to oversee cooling flow and manage UPS power. Finally, we present an improvement in the context of AO control commands, namely a more robust and reliable offloading of the optical corrections from the ASM to the telescope control system. Together, these upgrades support a more stable and efficient AO control under variable or adverse observing conditions.

Items.Authors: Kyler Kuehn, Bob Kehoe, Thomas Kelley, Chad Husko, Simon Ellis, Steve Kuhlmann
Items.Title: Advances in atmospheric OH suppression using photonic technologies
Items.Abstract: Atmospheric emission from hydroxyl (OH) molecules causes significant interference with ground-based observations at near-infrared wavelengths. However, narrow-band notch filters can suppress this background noise while maintaining robust transmission of light from astronomical sources. We have developed such notch filters based on photonic ring resonators, and have succeeded in matching the suppression wavelength to known OH emission lines. In order to incorporate such filters into effective astronomical instruments, however, we need to ensure that the internal light losses are minimized. We describe our efforts to improve the performance of these devices throughout the entire light path, including the coupling from input optical fibers, through the ring resonator devices, all the way to the detector.

Items.Authors: Gil Moretto, Kritsadi Thetpraphi, Mariano Moreno, Vincent Bruyère, Peter König, Johannes Hörber, Peter Rogin, Vincenzo Cotroneo, Varun Hemal Shah, Alejandro M. Paola, José A. Dieste, Maud Langlois, Peter William de Oliveira, Francesca Rebasti
Items.Title: Advancing and innovating technologies for the exo life finder telescope
Items.Abstract: The growing demand for astronomical imaging of faint objects, like exoplanets, and the need for earth observation from space require significantly higher angular resolution and dynamic range than current optical telescopes can provide. Mirrors are crucial components of these systems, but improving their performance involves substantial challenges. They must maintain precise shapes while resisting deformation from gravity and wind loads in challenging environments.  Under the Horizon (EIC) European Innovation Council's funding initiative, we are developing an innovative, lightweight, hybrid, metamaterial, and self-correcting mirror through the EIC Live Mirror consortium. This presentation will showcase our advancements in creating cost-effective, lightweight integrated optoelectronic systems and explore new remote sensing capabilities for both ground and space platforms, including the Exo Life Finder (ELF) concept for direct imaging of nearby planetary systems.

Items.Authors: Deniz Ölçek, Tore André Bekkeng, Fredrik Harring Mathiesen, Georg Magneshaugen, Halvor Strøm, John Rune Jakobsen, Vetle Berg Abrahamsen, Ha Hoang, Mattias Carlqvist
Items.Title: Advancing modular space avionics: design and development of an ADHA payload controller module
Items.Abstract: The Advanced Data Handling Architecture (ADHA) is an ESA initiative to establish a compact and modular avionics framework for future space missions. Within this architecture, the Payload Interface Controller Unit (PICU) provides centralized instrument control, data handling, and timing distribution. This work presents the design and development efforts of the Payload Controller Module (PCM), a key building block of the PICU responsible for sensor interfacing and payload command management. We outline the PCM’s role within the PICU, the motivation behind its modular design, and the progress toward its engineering model. The work demonstrates how ADHA’s reusable avionics approach can streamline payload development and support a broad range of scientific and Earth-observation missions.

Items.Authors: Helen M. McGregor, Dylan Simpfendorfer, Scott Smedley, Jon Lawrence, Jurek Brzeski, Roland Winkler, Andreas Kelz
Items.Title: AESOP: final performance of Aesop for4Most
Items.Abstract: The Australian Astronomical Observatory’s (AAO) AESOP project forms a key component of the Multi-Object Spectrograph Telescope (4MOST) system on the VISTA telescope. AESOP comprises a 2,436-fibre positioner, a supporting space frame, and electronics enclosures. The AESOP concept and AAO’s role in the 4MOST project have been detailed in previous SPIE proceedings.  The AESOP positioner has now been fully commissioned as part of the 4MOST instrument on the VISTA telescope. This paper discusses the engineering principles applied during the final assembly, alignment, and testing phases of the instrument.

Items.Authors: Kevin J. Kearney, Nicole Melso, Zoran Ninkov
Items.Title: Agile UV photometers for SmallSat constellations: a reference design for transient astrophysics
Items.Abstract: The rapid UV evolution of kilonovae (peaking <12 h), Type Ia supernovae (progenitor clues in first 3 days), and tidal disruption events (sub-hour variability) demands space-based, high-cadence monitoring inaccessible from the ground. We present an agile SmallSat approach using distributed constellations that enable 6–18 month development cycles, rideshare launches, and unique advantages: incremental deployment, in-orbit technology refresh, and graceful degradation.    Central to this vision is an open-standard Instrument Library of modular designs. We describe a compact 3-band photometer (deep-UV to SWIR) with a UV-optimized baseline built on proven near-COTS components, including LLNL monolithic telescopes (flight heritage: GeoStare SV2, Deep Purple PTD-R, SOHIP) and space-qualified sensors. We outline the architecture, key performance drivers, and a forward-modeling framework.

Items.Authors: Benoît Lecomte, Antoine Arondel, Bruno Crane, Jean-Pierre Dubois, Stephane Da Costa Vieira, Clémence De Jabrun, François Langlet, Dylan Le Claire, Gilles Morinaud, Marc Ollivier, Anne Philippon, Catherine Tamiatto, Xueyan Zhang, Jérôme Amiaux, Michel Berthé, Benoît Horeau, Jérôme Martignac, Norma Hurtado, Vincent Lapeyrère, Jérôme Parisot, Eitan Péchevis, Jean-Michel Réess
Items.Title: AIRS: alignment and validation of the infrared spectrometer of ARIEL
Items.Abstract: AIRS is the infrared spectroscopic instrument of ARIEL: Atmospheric Remote‐sensing Infrared Exoplanet Large‐survey mission selected as the Cosmic Vision M4 ESA mission. This mission will perform transit spectroscopy of over a 1000 of exoplanets to complete a statistical survey.   AIRS spectroscopic data will cover the 1.95-3.90 µm (Channel 0) and the 3.90-7.80 µm (Channel 1) wavelength ranges with dispersive elements producing spectrum of low resolutions R>100 in channel 0 and R>30 in channel 1. This article will describe the AIRS optical alignment method and results of the Engineering Model, providing important data for the instrument calibration.

Items.Authors: Federico Battaini, Luca Marafatto, Kalyan Radhakrishnan, Paolo Cerpelloni
Items.Title: Alignment sphere for opto-mechanical systems: new results and applications
Items.Abstract: Accurate alignment is essential for astronomical instruments with strict tolerances during AIV phases. We developed a metallic alignment sphere hosting a CMOS detector at its geometric center, improving stability over previous 3D-printed prototypes. Characterized via interferometry and portable CMM probing, the tool achieves sub-20 µm accuracy in locating the reference pixel, simplifying alignment by removing rotational degrees of freedom. Validated in laboratory setups, it enables rapid beam centering and focal plane materialization, supporting hybrid strategies that combine mechanical metrology with optical feedback. Designed to be employed in the AIV phase of complex-instruments’ subsystems, the sphere enhances precision, reduces complexity, and mitigates risk in high-performance instrument alignment.
